title: Written by the Finger of God

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When the Lord finished speaking to Moses on Mount Sinai, he gave him the two tablets of the covenant law, the tablets of stone inscribed by the finger of God." - Exodus 31:18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The long section of instruction ends with Moses receiving two stone tablets, and the description is remarkable: "inscribed by the finger of God." Not dictated to a scribe, not carved by Moses. God Himself wrote them. The words came directly from Him.

Stone was chosen for good reason. It lasts. It does not shift with mood or fade with memory. God gave His people something permanent and external to themselves, a standard that would not bend to convenience. His Word was fixed, and they could return to it.

But stone has a limitation, and the very next chapter will expose it. Tablets can be broken, and a law written outside a person cannot change the heart within them. Which is why God later promised something greater: "I will put my law in their minds and write it on their hearts" (Jer 31:33), a promise Hebrews applies directly to us (Heb 8:10). Paul told the Corinthians they were a letter written not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts (2 Cor 3:3). God still writes — but now He writes on us.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I treat Scripture as God's own words, fixed and reliable?
Is God's Word merely external to me, or genuinely written on my heart?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You wrote with Your own finger, and now by Your Spirit You write on hearts. Let Your Word not sit outside me but shape me from within. Write it deep in me. Amen.
